sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered why some variables work everywhere in your code while others don't? Let's explore variable scope!

• What variable scope really means
• Where variables can (and can't) be used
• How to avoid common scope mistakes

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine your variable is like a house guest:
- Some guests (variables) can visit your whole house (program)
- Others are only allowed in certain rooms (methods/blocks)
- If you try to talk to a guest who isn't in the room, you'll get an error!

Variables have boundaries where they can be used. These boundaries are called 'scope'.

• **Local variables**: Only exist inside the method where they're declared
• **Class variables**: Can be used anywhere in the class
• **Block variables**: Only exist inside { } braces where they're created

Key Points
points: A variable's scope is the region of the program where it can be accessed
A local variable is declared inside a method or block and exists only within that scope
Variables declared in a for loop header are scoped to the loop body
Two variables with the same name can exist in non-overlapping scopes without conflict
Accessing a variable outside its scope results in a compilation error

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Variable scope defines where a variable can be used. Always declare variables before using them. Practice identifying scope by looking at { } braces. Ready to learn about method parameters next.
